language.note: all three co-official; genuinely trilingual signage/media is routine, not exceptional

terrainDescription.zh: 北部厄斯林（Oesling）屬阿登高地延伸，丘陵森林為主；南部古特蘭（Gutland）地勢較平緩，農業與都市發展較集中。
terrainDescription.en: The northern Oesling is an extension of the Ardennes uplands, hilly and forested; the southern Gutland is gentler terrain with more agriculture and urban development.

plate.color: yellow background, black text, blue EU band on the left

roadInfra.bollardStyle: Black-and-white wedge-shaped bollards with grey reflectors, nearly identical to Germany's but with 3 bolts on the reflector instead of Germany's 2 — a subtle but reliable differentiator

utilityPole.transformerMount: Upside-down trident-shaped pole-tops are the most common style

historicalContext.zh: 盧森堡語、法語、德語三語皆為官方語言，日常招牌、媒體同時使用三種語言的情況並不罕見，是歐洲少見的高密度多語言國家。
historicalContext.en: Luxembourgish, French, and German are all official — genuinely trilingual everyday signage and media is routine here, making it one of Europe's most linguistically dense small countries.
